findings.title: Latest security workflow commit has Vercel failure due build rate limit
findings.evidence: Commit 9b1bb6477ce85dedd8d2c9170111b5e29cf8d709 reports Vercel status=failure with target upgradeToPro=build-rate-limit. Prior product deploy commit 2f9579031a01e94de1fcfd46a1c5bf9402917626 reports Vercel status=success.
findings.impact: The latest commit may not be live on Vercel. Security CI workflow code exists in GitHub but production deployment may lag until Vercel build quota resets or account is upgraded.
findings.reason_no_auto_fix: This is a platform quota/resource issue, not a code bug. Automatic code changes cannot safely bypass Vercel account build limits.
findings.recommended_action: Upgrade Vercel plan or wait for build quota reset, then redeploy latest main commit. Keep previous successful deployment as active until the newer commit deploys.

findings.title: Requested 10-minute autonomous cycle unsupported by scheduler
findings.evidence: Task scheduler rejected minute-based recurring schedule. Hourly audit task was created instead.
findings.impact: Continuous 10-minute monitoring requires external monitoring/CI provider or platform-native alerts.
findings.recommended_action: Use hourly ChatGPT audit plus Vercel/Supabase/Sentry alerts for real-time incident notifications.

findings.title: Enterprise demo mode was enabled by query parameter only
findings.evidence: The add-ons page allowed any authenticated user to request ?demo=enterprise or ?demo=premium and see Enterprise/Premium UI without an environment guard.
findings.impact: Users could confuse a visual demo with a real entitlement, creating commercial, support and product-trust risk.
findings.recommended_action: Keep NEXT_PUBLIC_ENABLE_ENTERPRISE_DEMO unset/false in production. Enable it only for controlled sales/demo deployments.
